title: Scalar defects distinguish precisely Brauer classes
statement: Let K be a field, A and B finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras, and x,y in its continuous degree-two units cohomology [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology]. Suppose R(A,x) and R(B,y) in the matrix scalar-defect relation [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect]. Then x=y if and only if A and B are Brauer equivalent (their positive matrix amplifications are K-algebra isomorphic).

source.place: The scalar-defect construction following Lemma 03R6, Theorem 03R7, and Section 0DVG

proof.text: Apply the forward implication to h : x = y to obtain IsBrauerEquivalent A B, and apply the backward implication to h : IsBrauerEquivalent A B to obtain x = y. The two implications are the strictly simpler directional components of the scalar-defect faithfulness statement.

proof_origin.document: internal decomposition of the scalar-defect faithfulness argument
proof_origin.place: composition of the two directional implications
